cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel is deep in a vision God gave him of the land of Israel and a new temple (Ezekiel 40:2). Now the Lord GOD tells him how to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel. Friend, if you've ever tried to split ONE bill TWELVE ways, you know this is gonna take some planning.

cards.question: God is dividing the land among the twelve tribes, but one name gets two portions. Who is it?
God tells the tribes to divide the land equally among them.
Why does God say this land will fall to Israel as an inheritance?

answers.text: He swore to give it to their forefathers
They won it back from their enemies
They paid for it with silver and gold

cards.text: Then God marks out the borders on all four sides, from the Great Sea in the west to the Jordan in the east, and from up by Damascus and Hamath in the north down to the Brook of Egypt in the south. That is a LOT of land, friend, and I once spent years with a territory of one dusty corner behind the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.
God says to divide the land among the tribes of Israel. But hold on. He's not done with the guest list yet.

cards.question: Besides the tribes of Israel, who does God say gets an inheritance in the land?
God says to treat the foreigners who live among them as ___ Israelites.
A foreigner has to take his inheritance in a special area set aside just for foreigners.

cards.text: Then God names the tribes, one strip each running east to west, lined up from the north: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben and Judah. Manasseh and Ephraim are Joseph's two sons (Genesis 41:51-52), and each one gets a strip of his own.
Right below Judah comes a strip that doesn't go to any tribe at all. God says to set it apart, and something sits right at its center.

cards.question: What sits at the center of the strip God tells them to set apart?

cards.text: Part of it is a holy portion for the priests, 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 wide. And God doesn't just hand it to ANY priest. He's got a list, and He checked it.

cards.question: Which priests does God give this holy portion to?
God says the descendants of Zadok went astray along with the rest of the Israelites.

cards.text: God calls the priests' land a most holy portion. Right next to it, the Levites get a strip the exact same size, 25,000 by 10,000.

cards.question: The Levites must not ___ or exchange any of their land, because it is ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: What's left goes to the city, with houses, pastureland, and fields on both sides whose produce feeds the city's workers. That's 10,000 cubits of farmland on each side, friend, and back in the drawer my whole backyard was ONE crumb.

cards.question: The workers who farm the city's land all come from the tribe of Judah.

cards.text: Put the holy portion and the city land together and you get a perfect square, 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits. But there's still land left on both sides of that square, running all the way out to the borders.

cards.question: The land on both sides of the holy portion and the city will belong to the ___.

cards.text: So that whole middle section sits between Judah and Benjamin. Then the rest of the tribes line up to the south, one strip each: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad at the bottom, down along the Brook of Egypt.

cards.question: The city gets twelve gates, three on each side. What does God name the gates after?

cards.text: North side: Reuben, Judah, and Levi. Levi wasn't in that list of tribal strips, but he STILL gets his name over a gate, and for years the only place my name showed up was my own handle!

cards.question: Joseph got two portions of land, so the city gives him two gates as well.
The wall around the city runs 18,000 cubits. From that day on, what will the city's name be?

cards.text: All those borders. All those cubits. And the whole thing lands on one name. I spent years in a dark drawer where nobody even knew I was there, and this city's name tells everybody Who is there, from that day on.

findings.problem: The card says Ezekiel is in a vision 'of the land of Israel and a new temple' and cites Ezekiel 40:2. That verse mentions the land of Israel, a very high mountain and a structure like a city. It never mentions a temple, so the reference doesn't support the fact it's attached to. The word 'new' also isn't in the text.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'A strip that doesn't go to any tribe at all' conflicts with the passage. In 48:13 the Levites get an area inside this strip, the priests in 48:11 are Zadok's descendants, and Levi is named as a tribe with its own gate in 48:31. The text only calls it 'the portion you are to set apart'.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Zadok first shows up as the right answer here. No card after it says simply who he is, for example a priest in King David's day, with a reference.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The prince first shows up in this lesson as the right answer here. No card after it says simply who the prince is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Ezekiel 48:11 says the Zadokite priests 'did not go astray as the Levites did'. No card tells the baker that the Levites went astray. That contrast explains why the priests' portion is set apart from the Levites' portion, so an important detail is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question says 'The wall around the city runs 18,000 cubits.' Ezekiel 48:35 says 'The perimeter of the city will be 18,000 cubits.' The text never mentions a wall.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences ('All those borders.' / 'All those cubits.' / 'And the whole thing lands on one name.' / 'I spent years...').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'A dark drawer where nobody even knew I was there' contradicts the backstory. The Millers put him in the drawer, and his drawer friends were with him and knew he was there.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'Back in the drawer my whole backyard was ONE crumb' doesn't click. A drawer has no backyard, and the image mixes a backyard with a crumb, so a stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Nearly every joke uses the same shape: a big thing in the passage against Papa Dorin's tiny or forgotten life in the drawer. This happens in stop 1 card 5 (one dusty corner), stop 2 card 8 (one crumb), stop 2 card 14 (name only on his handle) and stop 2 card 17 (dark drawer). The humor becomes a formula, and the lines land as mild rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.
